architectureDecisions: Digest spec (sha256 over canonicalJson from packages/agent-tools/src/run-trace.js: canonical key sort, undefined dropped): taskDigest = sha256(canonicalJson({id, repositoryRoot: resolve(repositoryRoot), baseRevision, prompt, verifications: [{name, command, args, timeoutMs}], requiredFiles: requiredFiles ?? []})) — the ORIGINAL declared task exactly as validateAgentTask (packages/agent-tools/src/supervisor.js) returns it, i.e. the prompt as declared, NOT the promptPrefix-materialized strategyTask that runSupervisedTask builds at dispatch (strategyTask = {...task, prompt: `${agentContext.promptPrefix}\n\n${task.prompt}`}); declaredContextDigest = sha256(canonicalJson({taskId, baseRevision, requiredFiles: requiredFiles ?? [], maxMaterializedBytes})); materializedContextDigest = sha256(canonicalJson({items: items.map(({path, sourceRef, snapshotRef, contentSha256: sha256(content)})), promptPrefixDigest: sha256(promptPrefix)})) over the resolveAgentTaskContext (packages/agent-tools/src/task-context.js) resolution — used:false maps to {items: [], promptPrefixDigest: sha256('')}; executionDigest = sha256(canonicalJson({model: model ?? null, permissionProfile, maxAttempts, maxFeedbackChars, timeoutMs, toolVersion})). Never hash or persist credential values: env is excluded from every digest and from the handle body. The V2 binding is persisted by persistRecoverableHandle in runRecoverableTask immediately after workspace/session creation and before harness.vary (first dispatch), then refreshed on every onActCompleted/onAttemptCompleted and terminal status write.

Versioned handle compatibility and resume validation order: packages/agent-tools/src/recovery.js exports AGENT_TOOL_RUN_HANDLE_V2; the handle body gains taskDigest, declaredContextDigest, materializedContextDigest, executionDigest and binds them inside handleDigest. resumeSupervisedTask gains the agentContext inputs (repositoryReader, maxMaterializedBytes, snapshotObserve) and validates in this order before any side effect: verifyAgentToolRunHandle(handle) -> read disk handle -> digest equality (else STALE_HANDLE) -> terminal-status check (else HANDLE_COMPLETE) -> tool.id equality (else TOOL_MISMATCH) -> recompute taskDigest/declaredContextDigest/executionDigest from the resupplied task and launch params -> re-run resolveAgentTaskContext on the resupplied task (deterministic: git show at the pinned baseRevision under the bound maxMaterializedBytes) and recompute materializedContextDigest -> any mismatch throws RecoveryError CONTRACT_DRIFT (covers changed prompt, changed verifier spec, changed requiredFiles/context content, changed model, changed permissionProfile, changed toolVersion, changed limits) -> SOURCE_HEAD_DRIFT check -> reopenRecoverableWorkspace. On success the identical promptPrefix is re-applied to rebuild the dispatch-time strategyTask, so resume dispatches the byte-identical materialized prompt (today resume never re-resolves agentContext and drops the prefix entirely — the original-versus-materialized gap). No same-id fallback: identity without the four digests is never resumed. Model and permissionProfile are launch fields carried in the tool invocation request (agentToolEnvironment in packages/agent-tools/src/tool-adapters.js) and are bound in executionDigest, so changed model/permission is drift, not an upgrade. Tool version is re-probed at resume (probeToolVersion) and must equal handle.toolVersion.

Configurable-limit policy, unchanged-resume retention and migration: the limit policy is exact equality, fail-closed — model, permissionProfile, maxAttempts, maxFeedbackChars, timeoutMs, maxMaterializedBytes and toolVersion must byte-match the V2 executionDigest/declaredContextDigest inputs; any change is CONTRACT_DRIFT, never a silent upgrade. Unchanged bindings retain the exact worktree (reopenRecoverableWorkspace, no second git worktree add), the same Core session (createFileSessionStore over recoveryDir/core-session with sessionId agent-task:<id>, then harness.recover(sessionId, {force: true}) — never harness.start, so no second lineage) and the same tool session (initialSessionRef: handle.toolSessionRef continues the adapter session). Legacy AGENT_TOOL_RUN_HANDLE_V1 handles fail closed with RecoveryError LEGACY_HANDLE carrying the migration instruction: 'AGENT_TOOL_RUN_HANDLE_V1 predates exact contract binding: dispose the legacy handle (disposeRecoverableRun) and re-dispatch via runSupervisedTask to mint a V2 binding; never backfill binding fields onto a legacy handle.' deliver-slice maps LEGACY_HANDLE to a quiet dispose plus slice reason LEGACY_HANDLE without resuming.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Canonical task and execution bindings (taskDigest, declaredContextDigest, materializedContextDigest, executionDigest) are persisted before first dispatch and revalidated before resume in the exact validation order; changed prompt, changed verifier spec, changed model, changed permissionProfile, changed tool identity/version or changed limits are rejected with CONTRACT_DRIFT/TOOL_MISMATCH before any spawn.
evidenceRequired: Drift-rejection fixtures in packages/agent-tools/test/recovery-contract-binding.test.js invoking resumeSupervisedTask with changed prompt, changed verifier, changed model and changed permissionProfile — each fails closed with CONTRACT_DRIFT before any spawn; resume re-materialization fixture: re-resolved agentContext yields the identical promptPrefix while changed requiredFiles/context content is rejected with CONTRACT_DRIFT; candidate-bound resume logs showing persisted taskDigest/executionDigest equality; discovery.json (EXECUTED_LOCAL_PROBE) is motivation only, not implementation evidence. Guards invariant 1 (exact digests authorize resume) and invariant 2 (drift fails closed before spawn).
